groups.title: Integrated gauntlet (brief, plan, native mutation, geometry, review, repair, report)
groups.detail: 26/26 case(s) passed, run twice with identical verdicts

cases.title: A complex brief becomes a composed screen with a dominant primary visualisation
cases.requirement: The reference screen's primary visualisation gets appropriate canvas area, the regions align intentionally, the supporting panels do not compete with the main task, and the composition does not collapse into a generic repeated-card template.
cases.detail: focal 'content' holds 33% of the canvas; 5 regions, 17 content calls, 2 metric card(s)

cases.title: The visual direction is applied across the frame, not only to the dark visualisation
cases.requirement: The reference screen keeps a restrained light surface system around one dark technical visualisation, and the direction reaches the whole frame. The data is declared as demo data, so no value is invented.
cases.detail: style 'technical-instrument' on 5/5 region(s); 1 dark surface(s) of 11; no invented values

cases.title: A new screen lands in free canvas instead of on top of the last one
cases.requirement: The root frame is placed in free canvas, clear of every frame already in the file, and the regions move with it.
cases.detail: the screen was placed at (3280, 0), clear of 2 existing frame(s)

cases.title: An asymmetric split view keeps the inspector fixed and the canvas fluid
cases.requirement: The inspector is a fixed width, the canvas takes the rest, the two share a top edge, and the inspector ends on the canvas edge.
cases.detail: canvas 816 wide at x=272, inspector 320 wide at x=1120, both at y=0

cases.title: A five-region dashboard with thirty items keeps every child inside its parent
cases.requirement: Every content child is contained by the region that holds it, the gaps between siblings are consistent, and nothing runs past the canvas.
cases.detail: 5 regions, 32 items, every child contained

cases.title: A diagram's edges resolve their semantic endpoints and survive a resize
cases.requirement: Every edge names two real nodes, the route touches the intended anchors, and the endpoints are recalculated when a node is resized.
cases.detail: 2 connector(s) resolved against their nodes; a second compile of the same diagram agreed

cases.title: Long identifiers and error strings stay inside their region at 390px and 1440px
cases.requirement: Long device names, model identifiers, paths and error strings wrap rather than run past the region they are in.
cases.detail: 8 text node(s) bounded at both viewports

cases.title: Extreme padding, gaps and nested sizing resolve to sane geometry
cases.requirement: Extreme but valid padding and gaps, nested fixed/fill/hug sizing, a narrow canvas and a large canvas all resolve without a negative or zero extent.
cases.detail: 4 extreme layout(s) resolved with positive extents

cases.title: Invalid input fails closed instead of producing a successful screen
cases.requirement: An unknown connector endpoint, a duplicate id, a malformed token, a negative size and an empty scope each fail loudly. A dry run or a successful compiler response is not a pass.
cases.detail: 4 invalid input(s) all failed closed

cases.title: The compiler keeps one coordinate space and reconciles the other
cases.requirement: Resolved geometry is page-absolute, emitted operations are parent-local, and the two are reconciled by a blocking check rather than assumed to agree.
cases.detail: the resolved box is page-absolute, the operation is parent-local, and the trace check agrees

cases.title: Every edge contacts the node it names, and a connector inside its parent is not a defect
cases.requirement: Both endpoints of an edge land on the intended node anchors within a documented tolerance, and the reviewer does not report the containing region as the endpoint.
cases.detail: the edge resolved to both device nodes, and the reviewer did not report its parent as the endpoint

cases.title: Seeded legibility defects are detected with targets and measurements
cases.requirement: A low-contrast nav label, a 10px operational label, a clipped identifier and a drifted repeated component are each reported, with the node they are about.
cases.detail: 2 review finding(s); contrast {"textColor":"#C9C6BC","background":"#FFFFFF","surfaceSource":"parent surface 'Nav'","ratio":1.71,"required":4.5,"fontSize":14,"bold":false,"layerName":"Cluster","proposedFill":"#7C7664","proposedRatio":4.53,"repairVerified":true}; the identifier is truncated and reported

cases.title: Legitimate patterns are not reported, and the thresholds are not lowered
cases.requirement: A status dot with the word ONLINE, a button with a sibling text label, repeated table dividers, intentional circles and off-grid diagram nodes are not defects. The WCAG AA thresholds are unchanged.
cases.detail: no finding against the 2 legitimate pattern(s); thresholds unchanged (4.5:1 / 3:1, 11px baseline)

cases.title: The review engine finds the seeded defects and leaves the legitimate patterns alone
cases.requirement: True defects are reported with their node ids, legitimate patterns are not, and the counts are reported against the seeded expectations.
cases.detail: 1 true defect(s) found with node ids, 0 false positives

cases.title: The reviewer tells a search field from a topology connector
cases.requirement: A placeholder inside a search field is the field's content, not a collision with a route. A label sitting on a real connector is still a serious finding.
cases.detail: the placeholder inside the search field and the two rules are untouched; the label on the connector is still serious and the icon button is still reported

cases.title: Intended containment is not a collision; every real overlap still is
cases.requirement: Placeholder-in-field, text-in-row, label-on-button, content-in-card and status-inside-badge are containment. An intentional overlay is intentional. Unrelated text overlapping, clipped text and a connector crossing content are defects.
cases.detail: 5 intended containments left alone; the stray connector and the overlapping text are reported

cases.title: A repair is proposed with targets, applied, re-checked, and its effect is measured
cases.requirement: A repair names the node it will touch, applies only to that node, is verified by a second structural check, and is classified as fixed only when the measurement changed.
cases.detail: one targeted repair, one named target, nothing else touched

cases.title: An unrepairable issue and a failed repair are not reported as fixed
cases.requirement: A finding with no safe operation is reported for a human, a repair that does not resolve is not counted as fixed, and a budget that runs out says BUDGET_EXHAUSTED rather than convergence.
cases.detail: no repair was invented, and the budget exhaustion was reported as such

cases.title: The real plugin bundle applies 15/40/62/100/150-op workloads and reports the timings
cases.requirement: Representative workloads apply atomically against the mock document, and the cold and warm latency, the stage timings and the node counts are measured and reported rather than assumed.
cases.detail: 5 workload(s) applied atomically; median apply 8ms, worst 29ms

cases.title: A validation failure, a mid-batch failure and a duplicate transaction all fail safely
cases.requirement: A bad operation is rejected before the document is touched, a mid-batch failure rolls the batch back, and a duplicate transaction does not duplicate nodes.
cases.detail: validation, mid-batch failure and duplicate submission all behaved

cases.title: Concurrent mutations against the same session do not lose or duplicate a node
cases.requirement: Two transactions dispatched at the same time both land, neither removes the other's nodes, and the document holds exactly the nodes the two transactions created.
cases.detail: two concurrent transactions both landed; the document holds 2 frames and no duplicates

cases.title: An empty, stale, missing or disconnected inspection can never report PASS
cases.requirement: An empty snapshot, a stale node id, a disconnected runtime, a missing render, a review failure, a geometry mismatch, a missing component, a successful operation with a broken result, an unresolved constraint and a skipped check are all reported as something other than PASS.
cases.detail: every empty or missing input produced a non-PASS outcome

cases.title: A render that fails after a successful commit is blocked, not verified
cases.requirement: A commit that succeeded with no render behind it is reported as an unverified visual check. The structural result and the visual result are separate, and neither borrows the other's verdict.
cases.detail: a successful commit with no render is 'indeterminate', not a pass

cases.title: A review that could not examine the screen is INDETERMINATE, never a pass
cases.requirement: A review reports the nodes examined, the rules evaluated and whether the scan was complete, and a result that could not judge anything is never a pass.
cases.detail: an empty, a truncated, a failing, an advisory and a clean review each get their own verdict

cases.title: A screen that cannot be resolved is an ambiguity, not a random selection
cases.requirement: A guard target that matches several frames is a question. A node id is used directly, and a name that matches nothing is a miss.
cases.detail: a node id is used directly, a unique name resolves, and an ambiguous or missing name asks

cases.title: Two consecutive builds of the same brief produce the same structure
cases.requirement: The same brief produces the same operations and the same structural verdict on two consecutive runs, so a failure can be reproduced.
cases.detail: 39 operation(s) and 5 region(s) identical across two runs

gaps.gap: The live evidence was measured against a deployment, and the deployment is not the repository
gaps.detail: The server is deployed and Figma loads the plugin bundle once, so either can be older than the commit the evidence names. The live group now says how many cases were measured against an older commit and how many cannot name their build at all, and the build-integrity group (issue #25) refuses the run outright when the recorded stamps do not name this commit. Redeploying the server and reopening the plugin panel is what ties the live evidence to the code.

gaps.gap: A golden is a regression reference, not an approval
gaps.detail: The goldens record what each screen looked like when a human looked at it, so a later run can be told that it changed. They do not say the screen was good: the review rules judge the screen, and a golden can only be stored through an explicit review (npm run goldens:update -- --approve).

gaps.gap: Text height is estimated, not measured
gaps.detail: The server has no font metrics, so a text node's height is a character-count estimate. The pipeline measures the width a text lands at, and a region holding text cannot be handed to Figma's own auto layout for that reason.

gaps.gap: The native path is covered structurally, not visually
gaps.detail: The native check proves the native path executes against the real Plugin API, builds a real auto-layout frame, renders it, and cleans up after itself. It does not compare that render against a golden: the native path is model-authored, so what it builds is not a fixed reference.
